pos.text:
A linear incremental idle game with charming pixel art and satisfying progression. I've unlocked about half the skill tree so far and completed the base game mode.

But here's the catch - pick the wrong upgrades or mismanage your resources, and you can genuinely break your run. No exaggeration. One bad choice and you're stuck restarting.

It's a polished, addictive experience with great visuals and a relaxing vibe. Just don't expect deep build variety or endless content - it's pretty linear and short.

One of the best incremental games, along with Tower Wizard, albeit this one is quite a bit longer.

It took me around 30 hours to beat blind, but it probably only takes half that time if you know what you’re doing.
Great art style. The music is serviceable for the genre and delivers a sense of progression with each run.

The last hurdle was quite tough to overcome, so most of that extra time came down to experimenting with different builds, which the game makes apparent is a deliberate design choice, given the many options for variety the prestige system offers. It might be subjective, but since you constantly need to switch up builds for different progression levels, this may put off some players, while others may love it.

Lastly, this is not a clicker game where you can max out everything and call it a day. You have to use your head a bit for once, but once you earn around 75%

So i see a lot of the complaints of previous reviews - and my point to contest them is that if you are playing this game to progress and finish as fast as possible then you're going to end up frustrated unless you already know some upgrades or look things up.

However - this game is truly incredible. Exploring what each upgrade means and discovering fun combinations on your own is a sheer joy, you can reset your meta progression points and try new combos between runs. The visuals, the music and the controls are super clean and smooth. I have 100% this game and i still come back to it, i play a lot of incremental and idler games and this is one of the very few i come back to most weeks. it scratches an itch that no other little incremental game has done in years. 

This game is worth the cost full price, and i eagerly await the end game update. I hope that this developer keeps going becau

The Gnorp Apologue is a fun, surprisingly short little idle game about beating the ever-loving crap out of a rock until you win. Solid concept, cute visuals, and surprisingly challenging - Gnorp takes what a lot of Idle games have (prestige system, rapidly escalating numbers, simple gameplay loops extrapolated to the extreme) and refines it into a solid, enjoyable package that never stuck around long enough to be irritating.

If I had to make one single complaint about The Gnorp Apologue, it's mainly just the title. Mainly the brackets and the lack of capitalisation. That's my only real bugbear about this game - everything else you pay for is solid, charming and entertaining - as difficult or as easy as your understanding of the game gets. It's hard to imagine anything I'd really change (except that title), and no problems were had as a result of it's visuals, sound or game design. Ove

(the) Gnorp Apologue is a clever incremental game.  What starts as a charming little game about tiny Gnorps hitting a giant rock quickly evolves into a satisfying sandbox of mechanics. Between tuning Runner-to-Mountaineer capacity ratios, scaling G.E.E.T. rocket engines, stacking dual-element status debuffs with Frostfire, or strategically holding back units to manipulate physical pile geometry, the theorycrafting is big part of the fun.  It respects your time, gives you synergies to solve, and feels rewarding when your setup finally shatters the rock on Compression 10.

It's a good game, bought it because I saw it recommended it quite a lot for incremental games. However I would say that a lot of upgrades / units you get are a little bit counterintuitive if you're trying to push the end game. They actively work against the goal you are working towards to beat the game.
A cute game where a single rock keeps all the shards for itself.

The game offers a generally enjoyable idle experience. Guiding small creatures toward steadily increasing wealth has a light, pleasant appeal. Watching the numbers rise creates a simple but satisfying loop, and the economy systems and building mechanics add a modest amount of strategic depth for an incremental. Progressing through different resource tiers feels reasonably balanced. The screen grows more cluttered over time, yet the overall presentation stays fairly charming. Strategy fans will likely appreciate the steady sense of progression, even if the experience doesn’t push far beyond familiar idle game territory.

I did enjoy this game, but I found myself not wanting to finish it for a couple reasons, the biggest one being the fact that a large section of upgrades and prestige options are useless, and if bought, they ruin your current prestige. If you are a fan of min/maxing and don't mind potentially looking up what upgrades to buy, you'll love this game, but personally I prefer an incremental game that allows for many play styles and doesn't punish experimenting. Additionally, I found myself just waiting for progress to occur more than I like to, but that's entirely a personal preference and not necessarily a game flaw. 

However, all this being said, it is a very good game and I would recommend people try it! The art style and premise are delightful, and I very much enjoyed gnorping it. The way they drew the rock shards piling up is extremely satisfying and makes one feel very accomplished when

neg.text:
This is a very hard review for me to write, because there is a lot to like about this game. Also keep in mind that my play time represents a lot of background game time, not active play (~15-20hrs).

So why a thumbs down? 
[list]
    [*]You spend a lot of time not knowing if your actions actually have a positive effect. This extends from minute-to-minute gameplay to the perk tree you make meta-changing builds with.
    [*]There are very few things to invest the idle currency into after the first few compression cycles. You spend most of your time waiting to get the special shards that spawn, or waiting hours so you can buy one level of something (because you can't see actual stats of anything) and not seeing any real effect on gameplay.
    [*]There is very, very little content to unlock in the game. By the time you've seen everything you will ask yourself, "that's it?".
    [*]There is

It was a fun game...when I was able to play it. I've run into an issue where the game starts and I can hear the Gnorps, but the screen is just blank. I've tried everything. I've uninstalled/reinstalled/verified game files. I've changed my graphics processor. I've set it to run as administrator. I've resized the window. I've deleted saves. NOTHING. I've found a couple community threads with this same issue and no updates. I'm really disappointed.

Starts off interesting, and feels more strategy oriented for an idle game, but when in the end, it really just wants to just be open for 20 hours and follow a very specific build to get to the end with no offline-accrual progress function (that I saw). If you vary off that path then you might be adding 5-10 hours to your end game just to reach the ending (again, with the game open in the background, no offline progress).

Feels like the game was padded with literally just running in the background with no input from the user. After 23 hours open of "playing" I feel like I barely got any skill points and have yet to unlock the last tier of skills. Not my type of idle game in the end.

I only don't recommend this game because this game would like to be linear but it just wastes time. Let's say you realize midway through a prestige that there was an optimal prestige point you spent. Well you cannot change it, and when you are so far into a prestige but you can't get another point, it just sucks to start over without gaining anything. 

There may be a few paths to win the game, but there are many things that just won't win you the game. If this game made it where you could win it your way, I would say that it's worth it. Since you have to win it using one of a few pre-defined setups (the ones the perk tree naturally guides you toward), I cant recommend it. 

Ran fine on linux tho

Descriptions of upgrades are not very clear, and the gameplay loop relies on too much afk to be enjoyable after a couple hours. Fun enough for those couple hours, but frustratingly slow to progress.

The Gnorp Apologue starts strong enough, but eventually settles into a grind that feels more tedious than rewarding. The core loop could be much more satisfying if progression were tuned down by 25% or more. As it stands, following guides feels like the most practical way to finish the game and move on rather than experimenting naturally.

The design philosophy is especially confusing: the game explicitly encourages you to participate but makes your clicks ineffective, and then asks to minimize it and let currency accumulate in the background, despite not being a mobile or free-to-play title. This approach makes the active gameplay feel oddly secondary if not non-existent.

The Gnorps are charming, but there is essentially no story to carry the experience, and the prestige perks are not compelling enough to sustain interest or encourage much experimentation after the initial novelty wear
Way too slow. Upgrades become too expensive too quickly and the game slows to a crawl. More of an idle game than an incremental one. Just needs to be rebalanced. An otherwise well made game.

I love this game, I think the progression is designed really well and the little Gnorps are so cute, but it's broken. For some people the game just doesn't launch, there is a pinned thread in the community discussions about it. The issue isn't universal but it is widespread. The workarounds all seem to involve launching it without Steam, so your playtime isn't tracked and you can't earn achievements.

This has been the case for years and has not been fixed. I can't recommend this game as a result, as much as I love it.

neg_longplay_50h.text:
This is a very hard review for me to write, because there is a lot to like about this game. Also keep in mind that my play time represents a lot of background game time, not active play (~15-20hrs).

So why a thumbs down? 
[list]
    [*]You spend a lot of time not knowing if your actions actually have a positive effect. This extends from minute-to-minute gameplay to the perk tree you make meta-changing builds with.
    [*]There are very few things to invest the idle currency into after the first few compression cycles. You spend most of your time waiting to get the special shards that spawn, or waiting hours so you can buy one level of something (because you can't see actual stats of anything) and not seeing any real effect on gameplay.
    [*]There is very, very little content to unlock in the game. By the time you've seen everything you will ask yourself, "that's it?".
    [*]There is

I dunno. It's cute, and its a bit of a puzzle game, but ultimately it gets annoying as progress grinds to an absolute halt when you hit certain points. It doesn't slowly trickle off into slower and slower progress as much as it is you play the game for ten seconds to buy some upgrades, then it slams into a brick wall. You're rather forced into prestiging rather than making a decision about when you want to do it. It's not unfun, but tbh I don't feel like my time was really well spent.
